description:
src/lib.rs:51 does 'pub use jmap_jscalendar_types as jscalendar;', exporting the ENTIRE public API of jmap-jscalendar-types under jmap_calendars_types::jscalendar::*. Today that crate is shared between calendars and tasks and contains only general JSCalendar sub-types — fine. But jmap-jscalendar-types is positioned as a shared foundation that other extensions may grow into; any new public item added there will silently appear in jmap_calendars_types::jscalendar without a corresponding decision in this crate.

Concrete risk:
  1. jmap-tasks-types-specific JSCalendar values land in jmap-jscalendar-types.
  2. Those values appear in jmap_calendars_types::jscalendar::* by transitive pub use.
  3. Consumers depending on jmap_calendars_types end up with task-y types in their namespace they cannot remove.
  4. Removing them later is a breaking change to jmap-calendars-types' public surface.

This is in tension with the workspace policy of cookie-cutter type crates where the difference between siblings should be 'the specific JMAP capability the crate covers, nothing else'.

Fix options:
  - Replace the alias with an explicit re-export list (already done at lib.rs:64-68 for the top-level names — just delete the alias).
  - Keep the alias but document it as deprecated and stable-but-no-new-exports.
  - Or: confirm that aliasing the whole crate is the intent and accept the coupling.

The docstring at lib.rs:46-51 already says 'New code should prefer the top-level re-exports'. The next step is to consider whether the alias should be removed (and the back-compat replaced by an explicit alias module containing only the same names as the top-level re-exports).

File path: crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/lib.rs:44-51
title: calendars-types: pub use jmap_jscalendar_types as jscalendar widens public surface uncontrolled
